title: X–XI. Form of judgment in four parts; end — God's glory — Cap. 13 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 1:6–7). subordinate ends stand as ye salvation belonging toward ye pious, ye casting off belonging toward ye impious, plus ye liberation belonging toward Christ's Church (2 Thess. The ultimate end belonging toward this judgment stands as such that God be glorified in his saints plus become wonderful in all who believed; XI. || Execution stands as in public plus solemn pronouncement, so such that ye just begin to enjoy beatitude consummately in heaven, plus ye impious to be punished without end in hell. The sentence stands as most joyful unto ye pious, most sad unto ye impious. 25:32–33. Separation belonging toward sheep out from goats stands as Matt. In knowledge ye judge needs no examination belonging toward witnesses. (4) execution belonging toward ye sentence passed. (3) decision belonging toward ye known cause plus promulgation belonging toward ye sentence; (2) separation belonging toward those to be judged; The form belonging toward this judgment stands as contained in (1) knowledge belonging toward ye cause; X.
pass_b_english: X. The form of this judgment is contained in (1) knowledge of the cause; (2) separation of those to be judged; (3) decision of the known cause and promulgation of the sentence; (4) execution of the sentence passed. In knowledge the judge needs no examination of witnesses. Separation of sheep from goats is Matt. 25:32–33. The sentence is most joyful for the pious, most sad for the impious. Execution is in public and solemn pronouncement, so that the just begin to enjoy beatitude consummately in heaven, and the impious to be punished without end in hell.

XI. The ultimate end of this judgment is that God be glorified in his saints and become wonderful in all who believed; subordinate ends are the salvation of the pious, the casting off of the impious, and the liberation of Christ's Church (2 Thess. 1:6–7).
source_text: X. Forma hujus judicii continetur 1. causae cognitione; 2. judicandorum separatione; 3. causae cognitae decisione & sententiae promulgatione; 4. sententiae latae exsecutione. In cognitione judex non opus habet testium examine. Separatio ovium ab haedis Matth. 25.32–33. Sententia piis jucundissima, impiis tristissima. Exsecutio in publica & solemni pronunciatione, ut justi in caelo beatitudine fruantur consummate, impii in inferno puniantur sine fine. XI. Finis hujus judicii ultimus est ut Deus glorificetur in sanctis suis & admirabilis fiat in omnibus qui crediderunt; subordinatus piorum salus, impiorum abjectio, Ecclesiae Christi liberatio, 2 Thess. 1.v.6–7.
